question: A shopkeeper professes to sell sugar costing ₹40/kg at ₹42/kg but gives only 550 grams sugar in place of 600 grams using faulty weighing machine. His profit percentage (correct to 2 decimal places) is:
solution:
**Given:**

A shopkeeper professes to sell sugar costing ₹40/kg at ₹42/kg

But gives only 550 grams sugar in place of 600 grams using faulty weighing machine.

**Concept used:**

If a seller sells his goods at a% profit on cost price and uses b grams instead of c g less weight, then his percentage profit will be 

[(100 + a) c/b - 100] %

**Calculation:** 

As per the question, 

the profit percentage is 2/40 × 100 = 5%

So overall profit,

[(100 + a) c/b - 100] %

[(100 + 5) 600/550 - 100] %

[114.54 - 100] % = 14.54%

**∴ The correct option is** 1
